description: The Wood Ox in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1925 and 1985 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Ox is the Ox born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the second animal. It combines the Ox's patience with Wood's qualities. Wood Ox years between 1924 and 2044 are 1925 and 1985. The Ox's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Wood Ox personality
paragraphs: The Wood Ox meets a lively challenge in its own chart. The Ox's fixed element is Earth, and Wood controls Earth in the five-element cycle, so a Wood stem is said to push and loosen the Ox's naturally settled nature, much as roots break up hard ground. Wood Oxen are often described as more flexible, sociable and forward-looking than other Oxen, willing to cooperate and consider new methods. They keep the sign's patience and work ethic but add a sense of fairness and a wish to improve things for others. The tension between Wood's urge to grow and Earth's urge to stay put can show up as inner restlessness, and Wood Oxen may feel torn between duty and change.

Wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak. Classical descriptions link it with kindness, idealism and a talent for cooperation: Wood people are often pictured as the ones who start community projects, mentor younger colleagues and believe that most situations can improve with patience and goodwill. The element also carries a strong sense of fairness and a dislike of waste. Its shadow side, according to most readings, is overextension. Like a plant reaching in every direction, a Wood-year person may take on too much, trust too readily or struggle to say no when a cause seems worthwhile.

sections.heading: Wood Ox at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

A Wood Ox brings stamina to collaborative work, the sort of person who stays after the meeting to finish the shared document properly. Teaching, agriculture, architecture, public service and running small charities are the usual suggestions, since each rewards patient building alongside other people. It copes best when its steady contribution is acknowledged and when change is announced early rather than sprung on it. In partnership the Wood Ox is dependable and rather more openly affectionate than most Oxen, happy to tend a vegetable patch, cook for friends or fix the dripping tap without being asked. It needs someone who notices these quiet efforts. Friction arrives when it shoulders everybody's burdens without complaint, then hits a stubborn, silent limit that nobody saw coming.

sections.heading: Wood Ox years and dates
paragraphs: Wood Ox years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 24, 1925 to February 12, 1926 and from February 20, 1985 to February 8, 1986. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1985 anyone born before Feb 20 is a Wood Rat, not a Wood Ox. Sixty years separate each Wood Ox year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Wood Ox year is Yin, matching the Ox's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Yi-Chou: Yi is the yin Wood stem and Chou is the Ox's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Rat year (before January 24, 1925) and the Wood Rat year (before February 20, 1985), and births in the weeks after each Wood Ox year ends belong to the Fire Tiger. The new year itself fell on a Saturday in 1925 and Wednesday in 1985.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Ox
paragraphs: The growth edge for a Wood Ox is learning to treat change as cultivation rather than upheaval. Readings suggest that this combination does best when it plans changes deliberately, one season at a time, rather than resisting until pressure builds. Wood Oxen may also take on other people's burdens out of a strong sense of fairness, so watching for overcommitment matters. Shared projects with clear roles tend to suit them better than solitary grind. Spending time outdoors, especially among trees and growing things, often eases the inner tug of war. When the Wood Ox lets its steadiness support growth, it becomes a dependable builder of lasting, useful things.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Ox shares the Ox's San He trine with the Snake and Rooster (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Rat, and its Liu Chong clash with the Goat. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Ox years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1925 (from January 24, 1925) and 1985 (from February 20, 1985). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Ox's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Ox's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Ox?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Snake and Rooster (San He) and the Rat (Liu He). The Goat is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Ox called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Yi-Chou. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Yi, followed by its earthly branch, here Chou for the Ox, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Ox different from other Oxs?
faq.answer: All Oxs share patience, diligence and steady strength. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
